sanskrit: tac chrutvā naradevānāṃ punarāgamanaṃ narāḥ jahṛṣur muditāś cāsann anyadehagatā api
english: Hearing of this return of the god-kings, the people rejoiced and were filled with gladness, even those who had passed into other bodies.

sanskrit: priyaiḥ samāgamaṃ teṣāṃ ya imaṃ śṛṇuyān naraḥ priyāṇi labhate nityam iha ca pretya caiva ha
english: The man who hears of their reunion with their loved ones wins what is dear to him forever, both here and after death.

sanskrit: iṣṭabāndhavasaṃyogam anāyāsam anāmayam ya imaṃ śrāvayed vidvān saṃsiddhiṃ prāpnuyāt parām
english: The learned man who recites this account of reunion with cherished kin, free of toil and free of ill, attains the highest perfection.

sanskrit: svādhyāyayuktāḥ puruṣāḥ kriyāyuktāś ca bhārata adhyātmayogayuktāś ca dhṛtimantaś ca mānavāḥ śrutvā parva tv idaṃ nityam avāpsyanti parāṃ gatim
english: O Bhārata, men devoted to sacred study, intent upon rites, joined to spiritual discipline, and steadfast, by ever hearing this parva, shall attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etac chrutvā nṛpo vidvān hṛṣṭo 'bhūj janamejayaḥ pitāmahānāṃ sarveṣāṃ gamanāgamanaṃ tadā
english: The Sūta said: Hearing this, the learned king Janamejaya was filled with joy at the going and coming of all his forefathers.

sanskrit: abravīc ca mudā yuktaḥ punarāgamanaṃ prati kathaṃ nu tyaktadehānāṃ punas tad rūpadarśanam
english: And full of gladness he spoke concerning their return: How can there be again the sight of the forms of those who have cast off their bodies?

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa dvijaśreṣṭho vyāsaśiṣyaḥ pratāpavān provāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭhas taṃ nṛpaṃ janamejayam
english: Thus addressed, that best of the twice-born, the mighty disciple of Vyāsa, foremost among speakers, replied to King Janamejaya.

sanskrit: avipraṇāśaḥ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇām iti niścayaḥ karmajāni śarīrāṇi tathaivākṛtayo nṛpa
english: It is established that none of all deeds is ever lost; bodies are born of action, and so too, O king, are their very forms.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni nityāni bhūtādhipatisaṃśrayāt teṣāṃ ca nityasaṃvāso na vināśo viyujyatām
english: The great elements are eternal, resting upon the Lord of beings; their union is everlasting, and there is no destruction for those that are parted.

sanskrit: anāśāya kṛtaṃ karma tasya ceṣṭaḥ phalāgamaḥ ātmā caibhiḥ samāyuktaḥ sukhaduḥkham upāśnute
english: Action done is done so as not to perish, and the coming of its fruit is desired; the self, joined with these, partakes of pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: avināśī tathā nityaṃ kṣetrajña iti niścayaḥ bhūtānām ātmabhāvo yo dhruvo 'sau saṃvijānatām
english: It is established that the Knower of the field is indestructible and eternal; for those who truly understand, it is the abiding selfhood of all beings.

sanskrit: yāvan na kṣīyate karma tāvad asya svarūpatā saṃkṣīṇakarmā puruṣo rūpānyatvaṃ niyacchati
english: So long as action is not spent, so long does its own form endure; the man whose action is exhausted assumes a change of form.

sanskrit: nānābhāvās tathaikatvaṃ śarīraṃ prāpya saṃhatāḥ bhavanti te tathā nityāḥ pṛthagbhāvaṃ vijānatām
english: The manifold states, gaining a body, are gathered into oneness and become joined; yet to those who understand, they remain eternal in their separate being.

sanskrit: aśvamedhe śrutiś ceyam aśvasaṃjñapanaṃ prati lokāntaragatā nityaṃ prāṇā nityā hi vājinaḥ
english: And there is this Vedic teaching in the horse-sacrifice concerning the slaying of the horse: the life-breaths pass eternally to another world, for the steeds are eternal.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hitaṃ vadāmy etat priyaṃ cet tava pārthiva devayānā hi panthānaḥ śrutās te yajñasaṃstare
english: I speak this for your welfare, O king, if it be pleasing to you: the paths that lead to the gods are heard of as laid out upon the altar of sacrifice.

sanskrit: sukṛto yatra te yajñas tatra devā hitās tava yadā samanvitā devāḥ paśūnāṃ gamaneśvarāḥ gatimantaś ca teneṣṭvā nānye nityā bhavanti te
english: Where your sacrifice is well performed, there the gods are favorable to you; and when the gods, lords over the passage of the sacrificial victims, are gathered, then by that worship those who move onward, and no others, become eternal.

sanskrit: nitye 'smin pañcake varge nitye cātmani yo naraḥ asya nānāsamāyogaṃ yaḥ paśyati vṛthāmatiḥ viyoge śocate 'tyarthaṃ sa bāla iti me matiḥ
english: This fivefold group is eternal, and eternal too is the self; the man of vain mind who sees only the diverse combining of these, and grieves overmuch at their parting, is a child—such is my judgment.

sanskrit: viyoge doṣadarśī yaḥ saṃyogam iha varjayet asaṅge saṃgamo nāsti duḥkhaṃ bhuvi viyogajam
english: He who sees the fault in separation should shun all union here below; where there is no attachment there is no joining, and on earth the sorrow that is born of parting.

sanskrit: parāparajñas tu naro nābhimānād udīritaḥ aparajñaḥ parāṃ buddhiṃ spṛṣṭvā mohād vimucyate
english: But the man who knows the higher and the lower is not driven on by pride; knowing the lower, once he has touched the supreme wisdom, he is freed from delusion.

sanskrit: adarśanād āpatitaḥ punaś cādarśanaṃ gataḥ nāhaṃ taṃ vedmi nāsau māṃ na ca me 'sti virāgatā
english: From the unseen he has come forth, and to the unseen he has gone again; I know him not, nor he me, and yet there is in me no aversion.

sanskrit: yena yena śarīreṇa karoty ayam anīśvaraḥ tena tena śarīreṇa tad avaśyam upāśnute mānasaṃ manasāpnoti śārīraṃ ca śarīravān
english: By whatever body this powerless one does a deed, by that very body he must inevitably reap it; what is of the mind he gains with the mind, and what is of the body he, the embodied, gains in the body.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca adṛṣṭvā tu nṛpaḥ putrān darśanaṃ pratilabdhavān ṛṣiprasādāt putrāṇāṃ svarūpāṇāṃ kurūdvaha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O foremost of the Kurus, the king who had not seen his sons regained the sight of them in their own true forms, by the grace of the sage.

sanskrit: sa rājā rājadharmāṃś ca brahmopaniṣadaṃ tathā avāptavān naraśreṣṭho buddhiniścayam eva ca
english: That best of men, the king, attained the duties of kingship and the secret doctrine of Brahman, and firm resolve of mind as well.

sanskrit: viduraś ca mahāprājño yayau siddhiṃ tapobalāt dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ samāsādya vyāsaṃ cāpi tapasvinam
english: And the deeply wise Vidura attained perfection by the power of his austerities, having drawn near to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and to the ascetic Vyāsa as well.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca mamāpi varado vyāso darśayet pitaraṃ yadi tad rūpaveṣavayasaṃ śraddadhyāṃ sarvam eva te
english: Janamejaya said: If Vyāsa, the bestower of boons, would show me too my father in that same form, garb, and age, then I would believe everything you have told.

sanskrit: priyaṃ me syāt kṛtārthaś ca syām ahaṃ kṛtaniścayaḥ prasādād ṛṣiputrasya mama kāmaḥ samṛdhyatām
english: It would be dear to me, and I would be fulfilled and resolved of purpose; by the grace of the sage's son, may my desire be accomplished.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ity uktavacane tasmin nṛpe vyāsaḥ pratāpavān prasādam akarod dhīmān ānayac ca parikṣitam
english: The Sūta said: When the king had spoken these words, the mighty and wise Vyāsa showed his grace and brought forth Parīkṣit.

sanskrit: tatas tadrūpavayasam āgataṃ nṛpatiṃ divaḥ śrīmantaṃ pitaraṃ rājā dadarśa janamejayaḥ
english: Then King Janamejaya beheld his glorious father, the king, come down from heaven in that very form and age.

sanskrit: śamīkaṃ ca mahātmānaṃ putraṃ taṃ cāsya śṛṅgiṇam amātyā ye babhūvuś ca rājñas tāṃś ca dadarśa ha
english: And he beheld the great-souled Śamīka and his son Śṛṅgin, and those who had been the king's counselors as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ so 'vabhṛthe rājā mudito janamejayaḥ pitaraṃ snāpayām āsa svayaṃ sasnau ca pārthivaḥ
english: Then at the purificatory bath the king Janamejaya, full of joy, himself bathed his father, and the lord of earth bathed as well.

sanskrit: snātvā ca bharataśreṣṭhaḥ so ''stīkam idam abravīt yāyāvarakulotpannaṃ jaratkārusutaṃ tadā
english: And having bathed, that best of the Bhāratas then said this to Āstīka, born of the Yāyāvara line, the son of Jaratkāru.

sanskrit: āstīka vividhāścaryo yajño 'yam iti me matiḥ yad adyāyaṃ pitā prāpto mama śokapraṇāśanaḥ
english: O Āstīka, this sacrifice is full of wonders—such is my thought—for today my father has been regained, dispeller of my grief.

sanskrit: āstīka uvāca ṛṣir dvaipāyano yatra purāṇas tapaso nidhiḥ yajñe kurukulaśreṣṭha tasya lokāv ubhau jitau
english: Āstīka said: Where the ancient sage Dvaipāyana, that treasury of austerity, is present at the sacrifice, O best of the Kuru line, by him both worlds are won.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ vicitram ākhyānaṃ tvayā pāṇḍavanandana sarpāś ca bhasmasān nītā gatāś ca padavīṃ pituḥ
english: A wondrous tale has been heard by you, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas; the serpents have been reduced to ashes and have gone the way of your father.

sanskrit: kathaṃ cit takṣako muktaḥ satyatvāt tava pārthiva ṛṣayaḥ pūjitāḥ sarve gatiṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmanaḥ
english: By some means Takṣaka was set free, through your truthfulness, O king; and all the sages were honored, beholding the destiny of the great-souled one.

sanskrit: prāptaḥ suvipulo dharmaḥ śrutvā pāpavināśanam vimukto hṛdayagranthir udārajanadarśanāt
english: A very great merit has been gained by hearing what destroys sin; the knot of the heart is loosed by the sight of noble men.

sanskrit: ye ca pakṣadharā dharme sadvṛttarucayaś ca ye yān dṛṣṭvā hīyate pāpaṃ tebhyaḥ kāryā namaskriyāḥ
english: Those who take the side of righteousness and delight in good conduct—those at the sight of whom sin falls away—to them obeisance must be made.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etac chrutvā dvijaśreṣṭhāt sa rājā janamejayaḥ pūjayām āsa tam ṛṣim anumānya punaḥ punaḥ
english: The Sūta said: Hearing this from the best of the twice-born, King Janamejaya honored that sage, paying him reverence again and again.

sanskrit: papraccha tam ṛṣiṃ cāpi vaiśaṃpāyanam acyutam kathāvaśeṣaṃ dharmajño vanavāsasya sattama
english: And the knower of dharma, that best of men, questioned the steadfast sage Vaiśaṃpāyana about the remainder of the tale of the dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā putrāṃs tathā pautrān sānubandhāñ janādhipaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ kim akarod rājā caiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Janamejaya said: Having seen his sons and grandsons together with their kin, what did the lord of men, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, do, and what did King Yudhiṣṭhira do?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryaṃ putrāṇāṃ darśanaṃ punaḥ vītaśokaḥ sa rājarṣiḥ punar āśramam āgamat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having seen that great wonder, the renewed sight of his sons, that royal sage, his grief gone, returned again to his hermitage.

sanskrit: itaras tu janaḥ sarvas te caiva paramarṣayaḥ pratijagmur yathākāmaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñayā
english: And all the other people, and those supreme sages as well, departed each as he wished, with the leave of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu mahātmāno laghubhūyiṣṭhasainikāḥ anujagmur mahātmānaṃ sadāraṃ taṃ mahīpatim
english: But the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, with but a small body of troops, followed that great-souled lord of earth, together with his wives.

sanskrit: tam āśramagataṃ dhīmān brahmarṣir lokapūjitaḥ muniḥ satyavatīputro dhṛtarāṣṭram abhāṣata
english: The wise brahmin-sage, honored by the world, the muni born of Satyavatī, addressed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who had reached the hermitage.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra mahābāho śṛṇu kauravanandana śrutaṃ te jñānavṛddhānām ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām
english: O mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, joy of the Kauravas, listen: you have heard the words of sages ripe in wisdom and holy in deeds,

sanskrit: ṛddhābhijanavṛddhānāṃ vedavedāṅgavedinām dharmajñānāṃ purāṇānāṃ vadatāṃ vividhāḥ kathāḥ
english: the manifold discourses of those grown great in noble birth, knowers of the Vedas and their auxiliaries, learned in dharma and the ancient lore, as they spoke.

sanskrit: mā sma śoke manaḥ kārṣīr diṣṭena vyathate budhaḥ śrutaṃ devarahasyaṃ te nāradād devadarśanāt
english: Do not set your mind upon grief; the wise man is not troubled by fate. You have heard the secret of the gods from Nārada, who beholds the gods.

sanskrit: gatās te kṣatradharmeṇa śastrapūtāṃ gatiṃ śubhām yathā dṛṣṭās tvayā putrā yathākāmavihāriṇaḥ
english: By the law of the warrior they have gone to that blessed state made pure by the sword, just as you have seen your sons roaming wherever they wished.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tv ayaṃ dhīmān bhavantam anurudhyate sahito bhrātṛbhiḥ sarvaiḥ sadāraḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
english: But this wise Yudhiṣṭhira waits upon your wishes, together with all his brothers, with his wife, and with his friends.

sanskrit: visarjayainaṃ yātv eṣa svarājyam anuśāsatām māsaḥ samadhiko hy eṣām atīto vasatāṃ vane
english: Dismiss him; let him go and govern his own kingdom, for more than a month has now passed while they have dwelt here in the forest.

sanskrit: etad dhi nityaṃ yatnena padaṃ rakṣyaṃ paraṃtapa bahupratyarthikaṃ hy etad rājyaṃ nāma narādhipa
english: For this station must ever be guarded with care, O scorcher of foes; this thing called a kingdom has many adversaries, O lord of men.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ kauravo rājā vyāsenāmitabuddhinā yudhiṣṭhiram athāhūya vāgmī vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by Vyāsa of measureless wisdom, the Kaurava king, eloquent of speech, then called Yudhiṣṭhira and spoke these words.

sanskrit: ajātaśatro bhadraṃ te śṛṇu me bhrātṛbhiḥ saha tvatprasādān mahīpāla śoko nāsmān prabādhate
english: O Ajātaśatru, blessings upon you; hear me, you and your brothers. By your grace, O guardian of earth, grief no longer torments us.

sanskrit: rame cāhaṃ tvayā putra pureva gajasāhvaye nāthenānugato vidvan priyeṣu parivartinā
english: And I delight in you, my son, as of old in the City of the Elephant, attended by you, O wise one, my protector who moves ever among those I love.

sanskrit: prāptaṃ putraphalaṃ tvattaḥ prītir me vipulā tvayi na me manyur mahābāho gamyatāṃ putra mā ciram
english: The reward of a son I have gained from you; great is my joy in you, and there is no anger in me, O mighty-armed one. Go now, my son; tarry no longer.

sanskrit: bhavantaṃ ceha saṃprekṣya tapo me parihīyate tapoyuktaṃ śarīraṃ ca tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhāritaṃ punaḥ
english: And as I gaze upon you here, my austerity falls away; yet this body, devoted to penance, is sustained once more at the sight of you.

sanskrit: mātarau te tathaiveme śīrṇaparṇakṛtāśane mama tulyavrate putra naciraṃ vartayiṣyataḥ
english: And these two mothers of yours, who feed on fallen leaves and share my vows, O son, will not long endure.

sanskrit: duryodhanaprabhṛtayo dṛṣṭā lokāntaraṃ gatāḥ vyāsasya tapaso vīryād bhavataś ca samāgamāt
english: Duryodhana and the rest, gone to the other world, have been seen, through the power of Vyāsa's austerity and through your coming together with us.

sanskrit: prayojanaṃ ciraṃ vṛttaṃ jīvitasya ca me 'nagha ugraṃ tapaḥ samāsthāsye tvam anujñātum arhasi
english: My purpose has long been served, and so too my life, O sinless one; I shall undertake fierce austerity, and you ought to grant me leave.

sanskrit: tvayy adya piṇḍaḥ kīrtiś ca kulaṃ cedaṃ pratiṣṭhitam śvo vādya vā mahābāho gamyatāṃ putra mā ciram
english: In you now rest the offering to the ancestors, our fame, and this whole lineage; tomorrow or today, O mighty-armed one, go, my son, and tarry no longer.

sanskrit: rājanītiḥ subahuśaḥ śrutā te bharatarṣabha saṃdeṣṭavyaṃ na paśyāmi kṛtam etāvatā vibho
english: You have heard the science of statecraft many times over, O bull of the Bhāratas; I see nothing left to enjoin upon you—so much has already been done, O lord.

sanskrit: ity uktavacanaṃ tāta nṛpo rājānam abravīt na mām arhasi dharmajña parityaktum anāgasam
english: When he had spoken thus, my dear, the king replied to the king: You ought not, O knower of dharma, to abandon me who am without offense.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ gacchantu me sarve bhrātaro 'nucarās tathā bhavantam aham anviṣye mātarau ca yatavrate
english: Let all my brothers and followers go as they please; but I shall stay close to you and to my two mothers steadfast in their vows.

sanskrit: tam uvācātha gāndhārī maivaṃ putra śṛṇuṣva me tvayy adhīnaṃ kurukulaṃ piṇḍaś ca śvaśurasya me
english: Then Gāndhārī said to him: Not so, my son; listen to me. Upon you depends the Kuru line, and the offering for my father-in-law as well.

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ putra paryāptam etāvat pūjitā vayam rājā yad āha tat kāryaṃ tvayā putra pitur vacaḥ
english: Go, my son; this is enough—we have been honored sufficiently. What the king has said must be done by you, my son: it is your father's word.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu gāndhāryā kuntīm idam uvāca ha snehabāṣpākule netre pramṛjya rudatīṃ vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Gāndhārī, he, wiping his eyes clouded with tears of affection, said this to the weeping Kuntī.

sanskrit: visarjayati māṃ rājā gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī bhavatyāṃ baddhacittas tu kathaṃ yāsyāmi duḥkhitaḥ
english: The king dismisses me, and so does the illustrious Gāndhārī; but with my heart bound to you, how shall I depart in sorrow?

sanskrit: na cotsahe tapovighnaṃ kartuṃ te dharmacāriṇi tapaso hi paraṃ nāsti tapasā vindate mahat
english: Yet I do not dare to be an obstacle to your austerity, O practicer of righteousness; for there is nothing higher than penance—by penance one attains greatness.

sanskrit: mamāpi na tathā rājñi rājye buddhir yathā purā tapasy evānuraktaṃ me manaḥ sarvātmanā tathā
english: Nor is my mind set upon the kingdom, O queen, as it once was; my heart is wholly given over to austerity, with my entire being.

sanskrit: śūnyeyaṃ ca mahī sarvā na me prītikarī śubhe bāndhavā naḥ parikṣīṇā balaṃ no na yathā purā
english: This whole earth is emptied and brings me no delight, O fair one; our kinsmen are wasted away, and our strength is not what it was before.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ subhṛśaṃ kṣīṇāḥ kanyāmātrāvaśeṣitāḥ na teṣāṃ kulakartāraṃ kaṃ cit paśyāmy ahaṃ śubhe
english: The Pāñcālas are utterly reduced, with only women left remaining; I see no one among them, O fair one, who might continue their line.

sanskrit: sarve hi bhasmasān nītā droṇenaikena saṃyuge avaśeṣās tu nihatā droṇaputreṇa vai niśi
english: For all were reduced to ashes by Droṇa alone in battle, and those who remained were slain by Droṇa's son in the night.

sanskrit: cedayaś caiva matsyāś ca dṛṣṭapūrvās tathaiva naḥ kevalaṃ vṛṣṇicakraṃ tu vāsudevaparigrahāt yaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthātum icchāmi dharmārthaṃ nānyahetukam
english: The Cedis and the Matsyas, once seen by us, are likewise gone; only the circle of the Vṛṣṇis remains, by Vāsudeva's protection—seeing whom I wish to abide, for the sake of dharma and no other cause.

sanskrit: śivena paśya naḥ sarvān durlabhaṃ darśanaṃ tava bhaviṣyaty amba rājā hi tīvram ārapsyate tapaḥ
english: Look upon us all with kindly eye; hard to obtain will the sight of you become, mother, for the king will undertake fierce austerity.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā mahābāhuḥ sahadevo yudhāṃ patiḥ yudhiṣṭhiram uvācedaṃ bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ
english: Hearing this, the mighty-armed Sahadeva, lord of warriors, his eyes troubled with tears, said this to Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: notsahe 'haṃ parityaktuṃ mātaraṃ pārthivarṣabha pratiyātu bhavān kṣipraṃ tapas tapsyāmy ahaṃ vane
english: I cannot bear to abandon our mother, O bull among kings; let you return swiftly—I shall perform austerity here in the forest.

sanskrit: ihaiva śoṣayiṣyāmi tapasāhaṃ kalevaram pādaśuśrūṣaṇe yukto rājño mātros tathānayoḥ
english: Here will I wither away my body through penance, devoted to the service of the feet of the king and of these two mothers.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tataḥ kuntī pariṣvajya mahābhujam gamyatāṃ putra maiva tvaṃ vocaḥ kuru vaco mama
english: Then Kuntī, embracing the mighty-armed one, said to him: Go, my son; do not speak so—do as I bid you.

sanskrit: āgamā vaḥ śivāḥ santu svasthā bhavata putrakāḥ uparodho bhaved evam asmākaṃ tapasaḥ kṛte
english: May your comings be auspicious; be well, my dear sons. In this way you would only become a hindrance to our austerity.

sanskrit: tvatsnehapāśabaddhā ca hīyeyaṃ tapasaḥ parāt tasmāt putraka gaccha tvaṃ śiṣṭam alpaṃ hi naḥ prabho
english: Bound by the cords of love for you, I would fall away from the supreme austerity; therefore go, my son, for little now remains to us, O lord.
